word.item: There were five girls and they went to gather firewood.
It rained heavily and they wanted a place for shelter.
They went to shelter and they found it was an ogres house.
They sheltered from rain and it got late.
When the ogre came it found them.
And it was happy, it was happy.
It asked the girls why have come here.
And they said we have come to shelter from rain it began to sing.
"Tinda tinda heavy rain tinda it has brought me girls tinda."
Those girls said, "We do not have ugali."
When they said we do not have ugali, again it went to the second one.
It went to the third one.
It went to the fourth one.
It went to the fifth one.
It told them, "I want to go with you to gather firewood."
"And as we are going to gather firewood. I want one girl to be carrying the firewood and delivering it."
"She takes home where we are coming from."
And while that ogre was with the children, it made a trick.
On those girls, it began on the first one.
It said to her, "Take the firewood."
When it reached, again it sang.
"Tinda tinda, heavy rain, tinda, it has brought me girls, tinda, now give me my ugali."
When one girl went, those ogres surrounded her children.
They surrounded and they surrounded, they took that girl, and they ate.
Again the second one went, and again he sang.
"Tinda tinda, heavy rain, tinda, it has brought me girls, tinda, now give me my ugali."
And the mother to these girls looked up and did not see her children, her girls.
One of the girls was called Shiyungu.
She sung saying, "Shiyungu woo, Shiyungu woo."
"It has brought me a loss, Shiyungu woo."
When that girl sang, she heard one of the girls crying.
When she heard her crying, she said, "Have you been eaten?"
"Put yourself together in the stomach of the ogre."
She left the stomach of the ogre and came outside.
The woman continued to sing that song Shiyungu.
The third one came, the fourth one came.
She tricked the ogre and said to him, "We all want to go."
She was looking for a way of escaping with her children.
Now, they went to look for firewood on the first day.
But on the second day, the ogre told one of the girls, "We will go together to look for food."
And the girl told him, "No, we will go together tomorrow."
Now, that woman took her girls.
She tied some onto her back.
She tied two of them into her arms.
And she put another one on her head.
She began to sing, "Shiyungu woo, Shiyungu woo."
"It has eaten my children, Shiyungu woo."
And she had her guards at home.
When the guards heard, they ran quickly.
They said, "Woman, you have found the children that the ogres had eaten."
They came quickly, and they fell on the woman.
They took her with these children.
They were filled with joy, and they went home.

There once was a hare a clever one.
He found a woman who was living alone.
He told her, "I want us to live together."
And the woman agreed quickly and said, "Oh, I do not have someone to send, I live alone."
The hare told her, "I will live with you."
The woman told him, "I have my farm I want you to go plough."
This hare used to leave in the morning, he goes.
When he returns, he applies mud on his feet.
He says to the woman, "I have really ploughed."
And the woman tells him, "Oh, my child, I have prepared food, it is here, eat."
The woman asked him, "You are ploughing, which crops should we plant?"
She told him, "We want to plant potatoes."
Hare left in the morning, he goes.
The woman counted months, she saw that the potatoes were ready for harvesting.
But the hare lied to her.
The hare used to leave and go to someone else's potato farm.
He dug big potatoes and brought for the woman.
She said, "Oh, Hare indeed you did a good job! "
And he too was happy and said, "Yes."
The woman prepared very good food and kept it for him.
The following morning he went again and brought potatoes.
The third time, he brought groundnuts.
The fourth time, he brought beans.
And all those things, Hare was just stealing them.
And the woman was so happy.
But on the fifth day, he owner of the groundnuts came to check and found someone was digging up his groundnuts.
He asked, "Who is digging my groundnuts?"
He went another day and found someone has dug beans.
He asked, "Who has dug my beans?"
The second time, he found he had dug up potatoes.
Hare continued to dug those things and steal, but the owner of those things built into that farm something like a ball.
He said to Hare, "Someone is finishing my things in the farm."
Hare told him, "I know how to fight with hands"

Hare said, "I will go, I will beat that person and kill him."
The owner of the farm told him, "If you beat him, I will give you 1000 shillings."

He went and beat that ball with his hand.
He hit with his other hand and it got stuck.

He kicked with his other foot, and it got stuck.

The owner of the farm, when he came, he found Hare stuck on the trap.
He took the hare and said to him, "So, it is you who eats my things."
He told him, "On this day, you will become meat."
He took him, and he said to him.
He called others and told them, "I have found the person who eats my things, I have caught him."

Some water, some fire, we want to eat meat.

"After I have died, then you slaughter me."
"Because I do not want you to kill me while I see."
They took hare to the rock.
When they threw him on it, Hare jumped.
He ran and jumped on the tree and said, "If I did not have my wisdom, I could have been slaughtered, I could be meat."
